This means splats with large covariances (large $\sigma$) that extend into neighboring cells are not indexed in those neighbors, which can lead to artifacts like "collateral darkening" or "visible wisps" if used for masking without additional fragment-level checks [S1, unofficial].

It explains that this indexing method leads to two specific artifacts when used for masking without fragment-level checks: 1) 'collateral darkening' because splats whose centers are in the carved cell are removed, but their ellipsoids contributed to neighboring cells; and 2) 'visible wisps' because splats whose centers are in neighboring cells but whose ellipsoids extend into the carved cell are unaffected. This directly supports the claim.
